key_insight: Autonomous labs need more than AI-generated hypotheses: they need executable experiments and measurable objectives. The paper argues for pairing large language models with bottom-up optimization to connect scientific ideas to physical actions.
problem_solved: Large language models can propose hypotheses, but hypotheses alone do not tell laboratory instruments what to do or how to evaluate success. The challenge is turning high-level scientific goals into actionable experimental workflows.
method: Use large language models to generate scientific hypotheses and high-level experimental goals.
Connect those goals to reward functions that guide bottom-up optimization.
Translate hypotheses into executable workflows suitable for physical laboratory experiments.
impact: For AI/ML practitioners building self-driving labs, the emphasis shifts from hypothesis generation alone to integrating objectives, optimization, and execution. This offers a conceptual path toward systems that can act in the physical world, not just suggest experiments.
visual_elements: Pipeline diagram: hypothesis → reward function → optimization → executable workflow → experiment.
Two-layer schematic pairing top-down LLM reasoning with bottom-up experimental optimization.
Feedback-loop illustration linking experimental results to evaluation and the next experiment.
Contrasting icons for an AI-generated idea and a robot executing a laboratory protocol.
paper_title: Enabling lab autonomy with reward functions and executable workflows
paper_authors: Sergei V. Kalinin, Boris N. Slautin, Yu Liu, Elham Foadian, Gerd Duscher
